title: Why was my git push rejected?

glossary.note: Your local copy of the server's main, updated only by fetch or pull.

glossary.full: A push that only moves a branch forward
glossary.note: The new commits sit on top of everything the server already has.

glossary.full: Replay your commits on top of another branch
glossary.note: git pull --rebase puts local commits after the ones just fetched.

key_points: git status compares with origin/main, your last fetched copy, not the server.
A push may only fast-forward: it never drops commits a teammate pushed.
Rejected? Fetch, look at what arrived, rebase on top, push again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Friday evening. Priya's cart fix is committed. One push, and the weekend starts.

out: error: failed to push some refs to 'github.com:acme/shop.git'

out.text: hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not
hint: have locally. This is usually caused by another repository pushing to
hint: the same ref. If you want to integrate the remote changes, use

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: Rejected? Exit code one. It says fetch first, but I pulled this morning.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: And status agrees with me. My branch is ahead by one commit.

out: Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by 1 commit.
(use "git push" to publish your local commits)
nothing to commit, working tree clean

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ahead of what, though? Ahead of origin slash main.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is not the server. It is Priya's local copy of the server's branch, a remote-tracking branch.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Git status never asks the server. Its copy is only as fresh as her last fetch, this morning.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: So the server may have moved. Let me ask it, quietly.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: Now status says diverged. One commit each side.

out: and have 1 and 1 different commits each, respectively.
(use "git pull" if you want to integrate the remote branch with yours)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Whose commit? The log can list what the server has and her main does not.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: Sam pushed his rate limit. If git took my push, his commit would vanish from main.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is the rule. A normal push may only fast-forward the branch, never drop work someone else pushed.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: Then my commit goes on top of his. Pull with rebase.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: And push again. Quiet mode prints nothing, so watch the status bar.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Exit zero. Next rejection: fetch, look at what arrived, rebase on top. Never force over a teammate.
